facts.value: At source level, 0.0f is passed as the final scalar argument to both item hurtbox renderers, each with a NULL matrix. xD0C selects ordinary hurtbox-state rendering when zero and numeric state/color-override rendering when nonzero, not transformed versus untransformed geometry. Zero also initializes all coordinates of the local model-display offset before owner checks and in the helper's absent/non-fighter-owner fallback. Attribution of these literals to this compiled section remains unverified.
facts.rationale: Corrects the transform interpretation and separates observed source flow from unproven constant-pool placement.

evidence.why: Both calls supply NULL matrices and zero scalars.
Override argument selects the color table independently of the matrix.

facts.value: The source-level hurtbox zero arguments are used for non-Unk4 items when b6 and b1 are set, x13 is clear, and configured hurtboxes are traversed. xD0C selects the ordinary or state-override renderer; both receive NULL matrices. The local position is zero-initialized whenever the model-enabled b7 branch is entered, before owner checks, not only when an owner is absent or non-fighter. The owner helper additionally zeroes it for that fallback case. These conditions do not establish compiled literal-pool placement.
facts.rationale: Corrects the overly restrictive zero-initialization condition and preserves numeric state selection.

evidence.why: Helper fallback and initialization before owner tests.

facts.value: Item-model rendering helper declared as void(HSD_GObj* gobj, s32 render_pass, Vec3* render_offset). The GObj supplies the JObj hierarchy, render_pass is converted through HSD_GObj_80390EB8, and render_offset is nullable and only read by this function. Read-only use does not make its declared pointer type const-qualified.
facts.rationale: Distinguishes the exact canonical signature from a possible const-correct interface.

facts.value: Consumes item kind and display flags, scale, facing, position, four hitboxes, configured hurtboxes, the numeric xD0C hurtbox display-state override, auxiliary rectangle and matrix data, and the special it_266F collision record. The pass selector is forwarded to each selected renderer. Hurtbox calls supply NULL matrices and zero final scalars; xD0C is not a transform reference. Successful helper results accumulate into a 0-or-1 output controlling the caller's graphics-state cleanup. Hurtbox callees may populate endpoint caches and set skip_update_pos.
facts.rationale: Corrects xD0C's semantic domain and records downstream mutations while preserving the established input/result flow.

evidence.why: Numeric palette override and cache updates.

facts.value: Implements diagnostic visualization of enabled item attack hitboxes, hurtboxes, special collision data and auxiliary extents, rather than collision detection or combat resolution. This rendering path is not entirely read-only: hurtbox renderers can refresh cached endpoint positions and mark them updated, without changing the hurtbox's collision-state classification.
facts.rationale: Retains the diagnostic mapping but removes the false implication that downstream drawing never mutates collision records.

evidence.why: Ordinary renderer writes endpoint caches and skip_update_pos.
Override renderer has the same cache side effects.

facts.value: It_Kind_Unk4 bypasses ordinary geometry and submits its special record only under b0 and either it_266F.x18 flag. Other items require b6 for the hitbox/hurtbox group, b2 for four hitbox submissions, and b1 plus clear x13 for hurtboxes. xD0C == 0 uses each hurtbox's own state palette; nonzero xD0C supplies a numeric palette/state override, except that an intangible hurtbox forces palette index 2. Both calls use NULL matrices. Rectangle and auxiliary-matrix rendering remain independently gated outside b6. Individual renderer pass checks can reject emission; any successful call leaves the accumulated return at 1.
facts.rationale: Replaces null/nonnull transform language with the verified numeric override behavior and preserves the exceptional intangible branch.

evidence.why: All item-level guards and independent branches.
Ordinary state palette and pass selection.

facts.value: The common callback gates model work on xDAA_flag.b7 and applies owner permission checks only under xDC8_word.flags.x13. Camera value 1 with xDCF_flag.b3 set submits three configurations, writing (b4,b5) as (1,0), (0,0), then (1,1); camera value 0 with b3 clear submits only (0,0). Other combinations submit no model. These display flags retain their last written values; configured bone-group show/hide operations are reversed around the first and third submissions without saving arbitrary initial visibility. The owner-displacement flag b7 is refreshed only in the x13 owner-preparation path, while the local position is initialized to zero before owner tests. Collision visualization runs independently, followed by graphics-state cleanup only on a nonzero collision-render result.
facts.rationale: Corrects the claim of temporary display-flag changes and documents persistent flags, unmatched camera branches and conditional owner-offset refresh.

evidence.why: Configuration writes and paired bone operations without flag restoration.
Conditional displacement refresh, numeric camera cases and independent collision cleanup.
